e: S3 Standard serves the reports while frequently accessed in the first week, then an S3 Lifecycle rule moves them to S3 Glacier (Flexible Retrieval), the cheapest class that still retrieves within 6 hours (standard retrieval takes about 3 to 5 hours). Deep Archive takes up to 12 hours, and Standard-IA or Intelligent-Tiering cost more for years of storage.

A Compute Savings Plan applies across instance families, sizes, and Regions, so it fits a company that changes instance types every 2 to 3 months, and a 1-year term gives savings. Reserved Instances and EC2 Instance Savings Plans are tied to a specific family or type.

Amazon Macie discovers PII in S3 using managed data identifiers, and it's enabled per Region, so configure it in us-east-1 and us-west-2 and run classification jobs. Security Hub, Inspector, and GuardDuty don't analyze S3 object contents for PII.

Both the SAP application and the database show high memory utilization, so memory optimized instances (such as the R and X families) fit both. Compute, storage, or HPC families don't address memory needs.

An interface VPC endpoint (PrivateLink) for SQS placed in the private subnets, with a security group that allows traffic from the EC2 instances, gives private connectivity without the internet. SQS doesn't use gateway endpoints, and placing the endpoint in public subnets or adding a NAT gateway isn't needed.

Create an IAM role with the required DynamoDB read/write permissions, put it in an instance profile, and associate the profile with the application instances, so the instances get temporary credentials and no keys appear in the template. Embedding or passing IAM user keys exposes credentials.

Amazon EMR processes large semistructured data in S3 in parallel (Spark, Hadoop) and can read from Amazon Redshift to enrich the data in the same jobs. Athena, Glue, and Lake Formation combinations don't provide the same parallel processing with direct Redshift enrichment, and Kinesis Data Streams isn't for moving S3 data.

VPC peering between VPCs in the same Region has no hourly charge and low data transfer cost, making it the cheapest option for 500 GB a month. Transit Gateway charges hourly and per GB, and VPN and Direct Connect cost more.

Cost allocation requires user-defined tags to be selected in the Billing console and activated from the Organizations management account, which applies to all member accounts in consolidated billing. Per-account activation or Resource Groups don't produce consolidated cost reports.

AWS Control Tower provisions accounts and OUs with a landing zone, and its drift detection and notifications report changes to the OU hierarchy and notify the operations team, with the least effort. CloudTrail trails, Config rules, or CloudFormation drift detection need more setup or don't track OU structure changes.

DAX is a fully managed, DynamoDB-compatible in-memory cache that lowers read latency to microseconds with minimal application changes and little operations. ElastiCache requires cache-population logic, and the Streams plus Lambda design adds more work.

A gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB, plus a route table entry for the endpoint, keeps DynamoDB API calls on the AWS network without the internet. Gateway endpoints don't use ENIs or security groups, and an EC2 interface endpoint is irrelevant.

The EKS Connector registers external (on-premises) Kubernetes clusters in the EKS console, so all clusters and workloads appear in one place with little overhead. Container Insights, Systems Manager, or EKS Anywhere as a hub don't give a central EKS console view as simply.

Client-side encryption with AWS KMS encrypts the data before it reaches RDS, so even database administrators see only ciphertext. Server-side or volume encryption protects data at rest but administrators with access can still read it.

Aurora is MySQL-compatible, so applications keep working, DMS migrates the database with minimal downtime, and Aurora Auto Scaling adds replicas as demand increases. Redshift and DynamoDB aren't compatible with the MySQL applications, and RDS only autoscales storage.

EFS provides a POSIX shared file system with a hierarchical directory structure that multiple Linux instances across AZs can mount and read/write concurrently with low latency. S3 isn't a file system, and EBS volumes (even io2 Multi-Attach) can't be shared across AZs or provide a shared file system.

API Gateway with Lambda receives the HTTP sensor data, and DynamoDB stores it, all fully managed and serverless, with independent components that are easy to extend later. EC2/Auto Scaling or a self-managed SQL Server on EC2 adds operational burden.

S3 scales to petabytes for storing the drawings, and CloudFront caches them at edge locations to cut load times. Glacier is archival, EBS can't hold petabytes with CloudFront, and ElastiCache or Storage Gateway aren't the right pairing.

EventBridge publishes metrics in the AWS/Events CloudWatch namespace, including MatchedEvents, TriggeredRules, Invocations, and FailedInvocations, which show whether the rule conditions match and the target is invoked. A DLQ only holds failures, and CloudTrail or Logs don't record rule matches by default.

An Auto Scaling group with a scheduled action raises the desired capacity to six every Friday and returns it to two afterward automatically, with the least operational overhead. Reminders or manual scaling need human action, and dynamic scaling reacts after load arrives.

ACM can't issue certificates signed by a specific third-party CA, so create the certificate with that CA, import it into ACM, and attach it to an API Gateway custom domain. Lambda function URLs don't support custom certificates.

Aurora Serverless v2 is MySQL-compatible and scales capacity automatically in fine increments (minimum 1 ACU is about 2 GiB of memory), handling inconsistent usage and unexpected increases with minimal administration. DynamoDB isn't MySQL-compatible, and provisioned Aurora or RDS don't autoscale compute.

Lambda SnapStart for Java caches a snapshot of the initialized execution environment, greatly reducing cold start and outlier latencies at no extra charge, which is cheaper than provisioned concurrency. Timeout and memory changes don't remove initialization latency effectively.

Aurora Serverless v2 scales capacity up for the 2 busy hours and down to a minimum the rest of the week, so the company pays only for what it uses, which is the cheapest for a weekly 2-hour workload. Provisioned Aurora, reserved EC2, or ECS databases run (and cost) continuously.

An RDS PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB cluster has a writer plus two readable standbys across AZs with a reader endpoint, giving high availability and extra read capacity in one managed setup. A Multi-AZ instance standby can't serve reads, DynamoDB isn't PostgreSQL, and cross-Region replicas don't add the same HA.
